focus: Explain step by step what the training actually taught students to do.

output.title: What the time management training taught students to do

scenes.narration: This video explains, step by step, what the training taught students to do, using the paper’s own description of the intervention.
scenes.layout_description: A simple title card with a student beside a checklist and an arrow pointing forward.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn student holding a checklist labeled with small boxes, an orange arrow moving from left to right, cream background, minimalist black ink line art with orange and yellow accents.

scenes.narration: The training was built around prioritizing, goal setting, strategy development, daily planning, and monitoring, all aimed at time management.
scenes.layout_description: Five small icons are arranged in a row, showing the training’s five parts.
scenes.visual_prompt: Five simple sketches in a row: a star, target, path, calendar, and clipboard, with orange highlights connecting them.

scenes.narration: First, students reflected on their current activities, including academic tasks and extracurricular activities, and wrote them down before judging their importance.
scenes.layout_description: A student sits at a desk with two piles of activities and a notebook in the center.
scenes.visual_prompt: Student at desk with two small stacks labeled by icons for books and hobbies, writing in a notebook, with a yellow circle around the notebook.

scenes.narration: They asked which activities were most important and why, then tried to identify the most important ones for their study goals.
scenes.layout_description: A thought bubble rises above the student, showing a few activities being compared.
scenes.visual_prompt: Student looking at floating icons of tasks, with one highlighted in orange and a question mark above it.

scenes.narration: Next, they defined concrete, challenging, and proximal goals for those important activities, and they set deadlines for what they wanted to achieve.
scenes.layout_description: A goal target and a small calendar sit side by side, linked by an arrow.
scenes.visual_prompt: A target with a small flag, a calendar page, and an arrow connecting them, all in black ink with orange accents.

scenes.narration: In the third phase, they developed a strategy for reaching the goals by listing steps, setting priorities for those steps, and planning how to start.
scenes.layout_description: A staircase of steps leads upward, with the first step highlighted.
scenes.visual_prompt: Simple staircase path with three labeled stepping stones, one orange-highlighted first step, and a student pointing at it.

scenes.narration: They also thought about possible obstacles and what to do to overcome them, while the training emphasized proximal deadlines for each step.
scenes.layout_description: A path with a small obstacle is shown, and a side note marks a near deadline.
scenes.visual_prompt: A winding path with a small rock obstacle and a tiny calendar close to the next step, with an orange arrow showing a workaround.

scenes.narration: The fourth part focused on daily planning, where trainees decided what they wanted to do and when, and built a concrete schedule for studying.
scenes.layout_description: A calendar grid fills the center, with a student placing tasks into time slots.
scenes.visual_prompt: Calendar page with small task icons being placed into boxes by a hand, orange circles marking chosen slots.

scenes.narration: They asked themselves which important tasks to concentrate on tomorrow, and where and when they would complete them.
scenes.layout_description: A tomorrow calendar page is shown beside a map-like workspace and clock.
scenes.visual_prompt: A calendar page labeled tomorrow, a clock, and a desk scene with arrows pointing to a study spot.

scenes.narration: Students also considered how much time should be scheduled for different tasks and how to avoid distractions during study time.
scenes.layout_description: A clock, a set of task blocks, and a crossed-out distraction icon appear together.
scenes.visual_prompt: Clock beside several task blocks, with a small phone-like distraction icon crossed out in orange.

scenes.narration: The last part dealt with monitoring task completion, so trainees checked each day what they had finished and what still remained.
scenes.layout_description: A daily checklist shows some boxes checked and one box left open.
scenes.visual_prompt: Clipboard with a row of checkmarks and one empty box, plus a student marking progress in orange.

scenes.narration: The paper says this daily monitoring helped students see completed tasks clearly, creating reinforcing information about their progress.
scenes.layout_description: A student looks at a checklist that visually fills up over time.
scenes.visual_prompt: Checklist gradually filling with checkmarks, a small upward arrow beside it, and a calm student figure.

scenes.narration: The authors also say the training was meant to help students deal with external demands through these time management strategies.
scenes.layout_description: A student stands between several outside demands and the training tools that organize them.
scenes.visual_prompt: Student surrounded by simple icons for work and duties, with a calendar and priority list creating order around them.

scenes.narration: Before training, students were asked about their learning history with time management, and most reported no or little experience.
scenes.layout_description: A small survey sheet appears next to a student with a mostly empty experience meter.
scenes.visual_prompt: Questionnaire page beside a nearly empty gauge, with orange highlighting only a small filled section.

scenes.narration: The training itself lasted 4 h and was given in groups of about ten students by one trainer experienced in time management.
scenes.layout_description: A small group scene shows one instructor at the front and several students around a table.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal group workshop scene with one trainer pointing to a board and about ten seated students, cream background.

scenes.narration: Students were told the procedure, their data would be confidential, and honest responses mattered, but the paper does not describe more detail.
scenes.layout_description: A consent-style scene shows a paper, a lock, and a student nodding.
scenes.visual_prompt: A simple consent sheet with a small lock icon and a student holding a pen, orange circle around the lock.

scenes.narration: The researchers measured outcomes directly before training, then 2 weeks later, and again 4 weeks later to see whether the training held up.
scenes.layout_description: Three time points are shown on a horizontal line with the training in the middle.
scenes.visual_prompt: Timeline with three dots labeled by small calendar icons, the middle one marked by a training symbol and orange arrow.

scenes.narration: They also checked whether trainees actually used the taught strategies after training, because that would help rule out a placebo effect.
scenes.layout_description: A student applies a checklist to a real study desk, linking training to daily work.
scenes.visual_prompt: Student moving a checklist from a training board to a desk calendar, with an orange arrow showing transfer.

scenes.narration: The paper’s design used one trained group and a control variable, demands, which was expected not to change after training.
scenes.layout_description: A split illustration contrasts the trained outcomes with the control variable staying steady.
scenes.visual_prompt: One side shows a rising and falling set of arrows for outcomes, the other shows a flat line for demands, all hand-drawn.

scenes.narration: In the results, trainees reported a significant increase in using the taught strategies between the first and third measurements.
scenes.layout_description: A simple upward arrow connects the first and third measurement points on a chart.
scenes.visual_prompt: Three-point line sketch with the last point higher, orange arrow rising from the first to the third point.

scenes.narration: There was also a nearly significant increase between the first and second measurements, showing an early move toward using the strategies more.
scenes.layout_description: A chart shows a smaller upward shift from the first to the second point.
scenes.visual_prompt: Two-point line sketch with a modest rise, a dotted orange arrow, and a small note-like symbol for near significance.

scenes.narration: For perceived stress, measured with the tension scale, trainees reported significantly less stress 2 weeks after training than before.
scenes.layout_description: A stress gauge drops from the first point to the second point.
scenes.visual_prompt: A simple gauge labeled tension with the needle moving downward, orange highlight on the lower stress side.

scenes.narration: Four weeks after training, the paper reports less perceived stress and more perceived control of time compared with the measurement directly before training.
scenes.layout_description: Two side-by-side arrows show stress going down and control of time going up.
scenes.visual_prompt: Paired arrows: one descending beside a tension icon, one ascending beside a clock icon, with orange accents.

scenes.narration: The control variable, demands, did not change significantly at either follow-up, which matched the authors’ expectation for this measure.
scenes.layout_description: A flat line for demands sits beside the changing outcome lines.
scenes.visual_prompt: A steady horizontal line labeled demands with no rise or fall, contrasted with nearby changing arrows.

scenes.narration: The authors interpret the training as helping students prioritize, set goals, plan their day, and monitor progress, which may reduce stress.
scenes.layout_description: The four main actions are gathered into one compact flow around a student figure.
scenes.visual_prompt: Student at center with four surrounding icons—star, target, calendar, clipboard—linked by orange arrows.

scenes.narration: They also note that students with no or little experience seemed to profit more, but they call the study preliminary and small.
scenes.layout_description: Two student figures are shown, one with a larger effect bubble, alongside a small sample note.
scenes.visual_prompt: Two students side by side with different-sized orange effect circles, plus a tiny note-like sample marker.

scenes.narration: So, step by step, the training taught students to reflect, choose priorities, set goals, plan daily work, and monitor completion.
scenes.layout_description: A closing summary card shows the five steps as a simple path forward.
scenes.visual_prompt: A clean path of five stepping stones labeled by icons for reflection, priority, goal, planning, and monitoring, ending with a small checkmark.
